I usually do not write reviews, but I feel this clinic truly deserves one.

If you are looking for the cheapest and fastest dental treatment, this place is probably not for you. However, if you are looking for highly professional, academically driven, long-term dental care, then this clinic is exceptional.

From the beginning, I could feel that their approach is very different from many places. Everything is based on proper examination, diagnosis, radiographs, discussion, and detailed treatment planning rather than sales or marketing. They do not push treatment unnecessarily, and they explain both the advantages and limitations honestly and professionally.

Yes, the clinic has many protocols and pays attention to details, but after experiencing the treatment myself, I now understand why. The level of professionalism, organization, sterilization, communication, and documentation is extremely high.

The doctor was very thorough and clearly focused on quality, function, and long-term outcome rather than “quick fixes.” I genuinely felt that the treatment was planned scientifically and responsibly.

In my opinion, this clinic is for patients who value professionalism, precision, and long-lasting treatment outcomes rather than simply searching for low-cost dentistry.

Very impressive experience overall.

text:
Before coming here, I honestly did not understand what a true dental consultation should be.

From my past experiences, a “consultation” usually meant lying on the chair, the dentist taking a quick look, and then giving a short explanation. That was all I knew.

But here, it was completely different.

The process began with a very thorough and structured examination. The doctor and team took detailed photographs of my teeth, performed comprehensive assessments using advanced equipment to evaluate the gums, nerves, and overall dental condition, and completed both small and full-mouth X-rays so I could clearly understand the full picture of my oral health.

What impressed me the most was what happened next.

Instead of a quick explanation, the doctor invited me into a consultation room and spent more than 30 minutes carefully going through everything with me. Every detail was explained clearly, patiently, and in a way I could truly understand. The doctor continuously encouraged me to ask questions, and even asked several times if there was anything more I would like to clarify, making sure I felt completely comfortable and informed.

Then, what surprised me even more—the doctor spent additional time summarizing everything in a structured and professional format, printed it out, and provided it to me as a complete documentation of my condition and possible treatment options and estimate price.

When I reflected on the entire process, I realized that the doctor had spent well over 1 hour of time, attention, and expertise only for this session. That level of dedication alone made me feel that the consultation at this clinic was truly worth it. and reflect their price.

At that moment, I understood something very important.

This clinic is not focused on rushing into treatment. Their priority is to ensure that the patient fully understands before making any decision.

For me, this level of care was truly impressive.

And now I clearly understand why this place is not comparable to typical street clinics in terms of pricing. The difference is not just in treatment—but in the depth of care, time, precision, and respect given to each patient.

If you are looking for the cheapest option, this may not be the right place.
But if you value clarity, professionalism, and a truly comprehensive approach, this experience is absolutely worth it.

For 1.5 years, I've been going to a dental hygienist here regularly for professional teeth cleaning. This was recommended to me in Berlin by the best dentist in Germany because of my periodontal disease.

Now I got a toothache and wanted to be treated by a dentist.

I was only allowed to have the treatment if I first undergo an expensive, comprehensive, basic assessment, including x-rays of all my teeth. They refused to check for cavities or the source of the pain.

The assessment then informed me that I have advanced periodontal disease and that my bridges no longer reach the gums sufficiently because the gums have receded, which is something they do all the time. This is causing problems at the edge of the bridge.

Yes, of course, that's normal in this case and I knew about it long ago.

One interesting fact: my pain isn't cavities, but plaque at the edge of the bridge, even though I had been there for a teeth cleaning 3 days earlier. But this plug hasn't been removed yet. So I'll have to go to another dentist.

Treatment options according to the dental report:
a) no treatment
b) periodontal gum treatment, which I've already had twice in Germany and can't be done a third time, as it doesn't bring the gums closer to the bridge.
c) new bridge
d) new all bridges

A receipt for my health insurance payment was initially promised, but then refused after payment because I didn't want further treatment. So I have to cover the costs myself, despite having insurance.

They're just trying to make a lot of money here; they don't care about the patient. It's better not to go.
